phc.inst.vitals-voice.summary: Say one number into one field.
phc.inst.vitals-voice.title: Speak a reading

khoj.description: Searches, answers, and proposes. It never commits: every write it returns is a proposal for a clinician to review and confirm on screen, exactly like every other write tool here.

lab.op.referral-accession.description:
Somebody outside this laboratory asked for a test. The accession desk records
who the patient is, who asked, and which panel. Nothing clinical is asserted
yet.
lab.op.referral-accession.summary: Register the referred patient and the panel ordered for them.
lab.op.referral-accession.title: Accession a referral

lab.op.report-release.description:
The report goes to the referrer. A released result is acted on by somebody
this laboratory cannot reach, so the release is irreversible: an agent
cannot propose it and a person has to tap an un-prefilled confirm.

fields.text: I attest the verified result is the one being released

lab.op.report-release.summary: Send the verified report to the referring clinician.
lab.op.report-release.title: Release the report

lab.op.result-enter.description:
A number per analyte. Each analyte carries three bands on its own question:
a plausible band that blocks the write, a critical band that raises
`lab.critical`, and a reference interval that is written down but that
nothing in the kernel reads.

fields.text: Reason for accepting an out of range value

lab.op.result-enter.summary: One value per analyte, keyed or read from the analyser.
lab.op.result-enter.title: Enter panel results

lab.op.result-verify.description:
A second person says the result is right. This is the separation of duties a
laboratory runs on, and it is the reason this operation exists as its own
step rather than as a checkbox on the result form.
lab.op.result-verify.summary: A second person verifies or rejects the entered values.
lab.op.result-verify.title: Verify a preliminary result

lab.op.specimen-collect.description:
The sample is drawn and labelled. From here the specimen, not the person, is
what moves through the laboratory.
lab.op.specimen-collect.summary: Record the draw, the sample type and its container.
lab.op.specimen-collect.title: Collect and label a specimen

phc.op.abha-link.description:
An ABHA is the patient's national health number. Linking one to their record
here is how a hospital in another district finds their history later.

fields.text: Patient consents to ABHA creation or linking

phc.op.abha-link.summary: Link this patient to their national health account.
phc.op.abha-link.title: Create or link an ABHA

phc.op.antenatal-measure.description:
The three numbers an antenatal contact turns on. How big the uterus is, what
the baby's heart is doing, and how anaemic she is.

They exist as a separate recording from the antenatal visit for one reason:
**a number is not a sentence.** The antenatal visit is dictated and lands as
narrative, which is the right shape for a history and an assessment and the
wrong shape for a measurement. A fundal height that arrives as the words
"fundus about thirty weeks" cannot be put on an axis, cannot be compared with
the last one, and cannot reach a district return. The same reading taken here
is a coded observation with a LOINC code and a UCUM unit, and it can do all
three.
phc.op.antenatal-measure.summary: Fundal height, the fetal heart rate and haemoglobin, as coded numbers.
phc.op.antenatal-measure.title: Record antenatal measurements

phc.op.antenatal-visit.description:
An antenatal visit. It asks for the history, what you found, your
assessment and the plan, and it does not offer the coded diagnosis
rows, because this build can code three conditions and not one of them
is obstetric. The whole of this visit travels as narrative text into
the published document, which is what that fallback was built for.

This narrowing is a fact about this build's vocabulary and not a
clinical judgement: terminology/condition-code.json holds three
concepts and says it is not a diagnosis list, so there is no obstetric
concept for a coded row to carry. It follows that this template codes
NOTHING. It is not clinically useful as a coded record until a
published obstetric list is signed off by a named clinical officer, and
it should not be mistaken for one. What it does do is keep the visit as
text in a record that reaches ABDM.
phc.op.antenatal-visit.summary: An antenatal visit, recorded as narrative.
phc.op.antenatal-visit.title: Antenatal visit

phc.op.consult-document.description:
The doctor's note. This is narrative, and narrative is the one thing ambient
capture is genuinely good at, because context recovers a dropped word and the
clinician catches the rest on review.
phc.op.consult-document.title: Document a consultation

phc.op.context-add.description:
A patient arrives holding paper. A discharge summary from the district
hospital, a scan report from a private laboratory, an old prescription from a
camp. None of it is ours and none of it is in our records, so today it is read
once at the desk and then it goes home in the same bag it came in.

This copies it in before the consultation starts, so the person writing the
note has already read it.
phc.op.context-add.summary: A letter, a result or a discharge note another facility wrote, copied in as given.
phc.op.context-add.title: Add papers from elsewhere

phc.op.delivery-record.description:
She has had the baby. This records it, and in the same act it ends the
pregnancy and starts the postnatal care she is owed.

Both answers to the second question -- a live birth and a stillbirth -- open
postnatal care, because the mother needs the same checks either way. A
mother whose baby was stillborn is at the same risk of bleeding, infection
and depression as any other, and a product that stopped visiting her would
be making a judgement nobody asked it to make.
phc.op.delivery-record.summary: The pregnancy ends and postnatal care for the mother begins, in one act.
phc.op.delivery-record.title: Record a delivery

phc.op.followup.description:
A return visit about something already recorded. It asks what has
happened since, your assessment, the conditions this visit is about and
the plan. It does not ask for an examination, on the view that a return
visit is usually about what changed rather than about a fresh set of
findings.

NEEDS SIGN-OFF. Leaving the examination off this form is a product
choice made without a clinician, and a follow up that does need an
examination has nowhere to put it on this template. The general
consultation asks all five questions and is the answer until a named
clinical officer confirms this narrowing or replaces it.
phc.op.followup.summary: A return visit about something already recorded.
phc.op.followup.title: Follow up visit

phc.op.handover.description:
A handover is a note with somebody's name on it. The nurse tells the doctor
what the mother said about the cough; the doctor tells the pharmacist why the
dose is halved; the ASHA asks whether to visit again this week. It is not a
transfer of custody and it moves nobody: the patient is where the line says
they are, and this adds a sentence to the visit.

It is deliberately back and forth. Nothing here closes a conversation, there
is no acknowledgement to chase and no inbox to clear, so a reply is another
note and the visit carries the whole exchange.
phc.op.handover.summary: A note on this visit, addressed to whoever picks it up next.
phc.op.handover.title: Hand over

phc.op.handover-reply.description:
A handover is a conversation, not a delivery. Somebody asked for something;
this is the answer, and it carries the state the asker needs to see: that it
has been picked up, that it is being worked on, that it is done, or that it
has come back.

It writes a comment and a state and nothing clinical. A repeat blood pressure
is recorded by the operation that records blood pressure; saying "done, 154/94"
here is a message about work, not a reading, and nothing downstream will treat
it as one.
phc.op.handover-reply.summary: A comment on the handover, and the state it leaves it in.
phc.op.handover-reply.title: Reply to a handover

phc.op.household-visit.description:
An accredited social health activist or auxiliary nurse midwife visits a
household and records the visit. This is the community half of the system and
the half that CARE was not built for, so it is ours to design.

fields.text: Household consents to this visit being recorded

phc.op.household-visit.summary: What happened at the home, and anything to follow up.
phc.op.household-visit.title: Record a household visit

phc.op.lab-order.description: The doctor asks for a test. The request lands on the lab's worklist.
phc.op.lab-order.summary: Ask the laboratory to run a test.
phc.op.lab-order.title: Order an investigation

phc.op.lab-result-enter.description:
The lab technician types in what the test measured. This is a number, and a
number entered wrongly here is acted on at district review months later
without anybody noticing it was ever wrong.

fields.text: Reason for accepting an out of range value

phc.op.lab-result-enter.summary: Record a bench result against the order it answers.
phc.op.lab-result-enter.title: Enter a laboratory result

phc.op.ncd-review.description:
A review of a condition somebody is already being treated for. It asks
the same five things the general consultation asks, and it will not
commit without what you found on examination, because a review whose
measurements are missing is a visit nobody can compare the next one to.

NEEDS SIGN-OFF. That the examination is required here, rather than
optional as it is on the general consultation, is a product choice made
without a clinician. It states no interval, no target and no threshold,
and it must not be read as a review protocol. A named clinical officer
has to confirm it before this template is offered to anybody.
phc.op.ncd-review.summary: A review visit for a condition already being treated.
phc.op.ncd-review.title: Review a long term condition

phc.op.patient-register.description:
Make a new patient record. This is the second thing the clerk does, never the
first. The first thing is always to search.
phc.op.patient-register.summary: Create a record for a patient the facility has not seen before.
phc.op.patient-register.title: Register a new patient

phc.op.pharmacy-dispense.description:
The pharmacist hands over medicine and records it. What gets recorded is what
the patient was actually given, which is not always what the doctor wrote.
Stockouts at a primary health centre are routine, so a partial dispense is a
normal outcome and not an error.
phc.op.pharmacy-dispense.summary: Record what was handed over, and drop stock by that much.
phc.op.pharmacy-dispense.title: Dispense a prescription

phc.op.postnatal-close.description:
Her postnatal care is finished, or it is not going to happen, and this says
so. The home visits still owed stop the moment it lands.
phc.op.postnatal-close.summary: Postnatal care is over, and every home visit still owed stops.
phc.op.postnatal-close.title: Close postnatal care

phc.op.postnatal-visit.description:
Somebody went to the house. This is what says so, and it is what closes one
of the seven contacts in `bundles/phc/phc.sched.postnatal.md`.

Nobody at home is an answer. A visit that was made and found an empty house
is not the same as a visit nobody made, and a schedule that cannot tell them
apart sends the same person back tomorrow and blames her for the gap.
phc.op.postnatal-visit.summary: Somebody went to the house in the six weeks after she delivered.
phc.op.postnatal-visit.title: Record a postnatal home visit

phc.op.pregnancy-close.description:
The pregnancy is over, however it ended, and this is what says so. It is
the most important operation in the maternal half of this product, and not
because of what it records.

It is important because of what it STOPS.
phc.op.pregnancy-close.summary: Record how the pregnancy ended, and stop everything still scheduled for it.
phc.op.pregnancy-close.title: Close a pregnancy record

phc.op.pregnancy-open.description:
A woman is pregnant and this centre is going to follow her for nine months.
This is the record that says so, and it is the thing every later date hangs
off.

It exists because a thread is one visit. A visit is the right unit for the
guard, which asks questions about what has happened here today, and it is
the wrong unit for a pregnancy, which has a start, a sequence of contacts
and an end. A flat list of a woman's visits cannot say which of them belong
to this pregnancy, cannot carry the date the sequence is measured from, and
cannot END, so nothing derived from it can ever stop.
phc.op.pregnancy-open.summary: Open the pregnancy this centre will follow, and the date it is measured from.
phc.op.pregnancy-open.title: Start a pregnancy record

phc.op.referral-close.description:
Somebody found out what happened to a woman who was sent on, and this is
where they say so. It is the second half of "every referral closed".
phc.op.referral-close.summary: Record what happened to a referral, and stop chasing it.
phc.op.referral-close.title: Close a referral

phc.op.referral-raise.description:
The centre cannot do what this woman needs, so she is sent on. The
referral stays open from that moment until somebody records what happened
to her, and while it is open it is something this centre owes.

Hera's line is "every voice heard, every referral closed", and this is the
first half of the second clause.
phc.op.referral-raise.summary: Send her somewhere else, and keep the referral open until somebody closes it.
phc.op.referral-raise.title: Refer this patient onward

phc.op.risk-mark.description:
A woman's pregnancy is judged high risk. This records the risk factor
found and the date, and from that day she is owed three extra check-ups
with a doctor, over and above her ordinary four.

fields.text: Date she is marked high risk

phc.op.risk-mark.summary: Record the risk factor found, and open the three extra check-ups it earns.
phc.op.risk-mark.title: Mark a pregnancy high risk

phc.op.rx-prescribe.description:
The doctor prescribes. Confirming the prescription is what makes the
pharmacist's dispense action exist at all.
phc.op.rx-prescribe.summary: Prescribe medicines, with pharmacy stock in view.
phc.op.rx-prescribe.title: Write a prescription

phc.op.vitals-record.description:
The nurse takes the patient's readings and records them. These are numbers,
and they travel: an abnormal blood pressure recorded here becomes a district
level statistic and a treatment decision.
phc.op.vitals-record.summary: Blood pressure, oxygen saturation, weight and temperature.
phc.op.vitals-record.title: Record vitals and triage

phc.sched.antenatal.title: Antenatal contacts

nudges.say: Five people in the house, two under five.
The youngest has not had her measles dose.
There is standing water behind the house.
Burning when she passes urine, four days now.
Diabetic for six years, on metformin.
Chest is clear, no tenderness in the abdomen.
This looks like a urinary tract infection.
Nitrofurantoin hundred milligrams, twice a day, five days.
Send a urine routine and a blood sugar.
Plenty of water, and come back if the fever climbs.
Review her in one week.
Refer her to the district hospital for a scan.
BP one twenty over eighty, pulse eighty four.
Temperature ninety nine point four, weight fifty one kilos.
Fever since three days, and a cough at night.
She is breathless, send her in first.
Her name is Sunita Devi, she is thirty two.
Mobile nine eight four one two three four five six.
She has come from Barkagaon.
She already has an ABHA number.
